title: Plugin Maker Helper
intro: This page is switches and drop-downs only: turn on the master switch, then press /plugin in any GCP-AI chat (or click the floating hint above the input box) and tell the AI what plugin you want.
sec_switch_desc: When off, create_plugin refuses to run and nothing is written into plugins/.
switch_hint_on: Ready: type /plugin in any GCP-AI chat, or click the floating hint above the input box.
switch_hint_off: Generation is off: turn this switch on and the AI can use create_plugin again.
switch_save_failed: The setting could not be saved (the settings file may be read-only). This change only applies to the current page.
sec_skill_desc: These rules are an internal component of Plugin Maker Helper, not a separate plugin; only the rules you leave on are written into the /plugin directive.
skill_require_readme_desc: Force every new plugin to ship documentation. Turn it off and the skeleton has no README.md.
skill_readme_strict_desc: Core features, install & usage, folder layout, settings, pitfalls and how to extend it — every section, no one-line cop-outs.
skill_three_languages_desc: New plugins carry Simplified Chinese / Traditional Chinese / English strings that the user can switch between.
skill_readme_zh_TW_desc: In addition to README.md, produce a separate Traditional-Chinese document. (off by default)
skill_readme_en_US_desc: In addition to README.md, produce a separate English document. (off by default)
skill_default_language_desc: Unless the AI is told otherwise in the conversation, new plugins are written in this language.
how_line1: 1. Turn on the master switch above.
how_line2: 2. Type /plugin in any GCP-AI chat (or just click the floating hint above the input box).
how_line3: 3. Tell the AI what plugin you want — it calls create_plugin, installs it, and you switch it on in the plugin center.
hint_label: let AI build a plugin for you
hint_prompt:
The user wants Plugin Maker Helper to build them a **new ToolsGCP plugin** (their message starts with /plugin; the requirement is in the conversation).

Do it in this order:
1. Work out from the conversation what the plugin should do (one sentence), give it a display name, and pick a plugin id.
   · The id may only contain **lowercase letters, digits and hyphens**, 2-41 characters, starting with a letter or digit (e.g. clip-cleaner).
   · Do not use the reserved names _template, plugin-showcase or gcp-plugin-maker, and do not start with _ or a dot.
2. Call the `create_plugin` tool with id, name (display name), idea (one sentence on what it does) and language (use {language} when the user did not say).
3. If the tool returns ok=false, relay its error text verbatim and explain how to fix it (pick another id, turn on the Plugin Maker Helper master switch, ...). Never pretend it succeeded.
4. If the tool returns ok=true, tell the user the plugin is installed: it is **disabled** by default in the plugin center, so they only need to switch it on; also give them the folder path from the result.
5. Then implement the feature completely, following the Skill rules below.

[The user's own words win]
Anything the user explicitly asked for in the conversation (language, no README, README in English, ...) outranks every Skill rule below; use the rules only where the user said nothing.

[Skill rules currently enabled (from core/skill.py; the rule text itself is Chinese)]
{rules}
tool_desc: Write a new ToolsGCP plugin skeleton into this machine's plugins/ folder and make it appear in the plugin center right away. Arguments: id (2-41 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit), name (display name), idea (one sentence on what the plugin does), language (optional; defaults to the development language chosen in Plugin Maker Helper). If the Plugin Maker Helper master switch is off, this tool refuses and tells you why.
tool_disabled: Plugin Maker Helper is not enabled (turn on the master switch on its settings page)
